interface.name: aximos_shell_v1

description.summary: what AximOS's desktop does beyond Wayland's own

interface.description: libgui's apps use it for what wm does that Wayland has no protocol for: notifications, blur behind see-through windows, the screen's size and scale, settings changing, and the log-in screen unlocking the desktop.

request.name: set_translucent

description.summary: blur what's under the window through its pixels

request.description: With it on, wm shows what's under the surface blurred, as much as each pixel's alpha leaves it see-through.

request.name: notify
request.description: From the window it's about, if any, whose icon it gets. With a label, it has a button that runs command, as Super+R would.

description.summary: the settings were saved, so wm and every app load them again
from the log-in or lock screen wm started, once someone's in

event.name: screen

description.summary: the desktop's size, in its own pixels

event.description: Sent on binding and whenever it changes. The screen's pixels are scale times as wide and high, and can_set_mode is 1 if its resolution can change.
